name: Astana
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Astana: AIFC counterparties, state-linked contracts, ownership research and support for AIFC disputes.
hero_lede: Astana is Kazakhstan's capital, seat of government and home of the Astana International Financial Centre, with its common law court and arbitration centre. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching Astana, using lawful sources and coordinating Kazakh counsel and qualified local professionals where local work is required.
intro: Astana had 1,668,750 residents on 1 May 2026 according to the Bureau of National Statistics, and its gross regional product reached about 18.9 trillion tenge in 2025, around 11.9 percent of national GDP, with real growth of 11.6 percent. The economy is built around the state: ministries, parliament, the Supreme Court and the agencies that award contracts and licences are based here. Construction and manufacturing have grown quickly, with industrial output of about 1.6 trillion tenge in the first five months of 2026 and new industrial parks and energy projects, some with Chinese partners. The Astana International Financial Centre had more than 4,900 registered companies from over 90 countries by the end of 2025.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Astana because it is where government decisions, state-linked capital and international finance meet. Foreign investors and contractors bidding for infrastructure, energy and public projects need to understand the companies and individuals on the other side, including links to officials and their families. Funds, banks, fintech and digital asset firms licensed in the AIFC attract counterparty and partnership diligence, and the AIFC Court and International Arbitration Centre generate disputes requiring evidence and asset research. Kazakhstan's role as a transit and trade partner between China, Russia and Europe adds sanctions and export control questions for Astana companies dealing in controlled goods.

matters.title: Public contract counterparty research
matters.text: Foreign contractors and investors in Astana infrastructure, energy and public projects need to know who stands behind local partners and subcontractors. We research ownership, management, affiliations with officials and their relatives, litigation and media, supporting anti-corruption compliance under home-country laws.

matters.title: AIFC participant due diligence
matters.text: Thousands of funds, asset managers, fintech and digital asset firms are registered in the AIFC. We research the principals, licensing history, regulatory actions, related companies outside the AIFC and adverse media for participants, before investment, partnership or correspondent relationships are agreed.

matters.title: Evidence for AIFC disputes
matters.text: Parties before the AIFC Court or International Arbitration Centre need facts about counterparties, their assets and their conduct. We provide documented research on corporate histories, related parties and asset indications in Kazakhstan and abroad, prepared for use by counsel under the forum's English-language procedures.

matters.title: Sanctions and diversion screening
matters.text: Astana trading and industrial companies may sit in supply chains connecting China, Russia and Europe. We research ownership, management, trading patterns visible in public sources and links to restricted parties, so exporters and banks can assess diversion risk before shipping controlled goods or processing payments.

matters.title: Ownership of state-linked groups
matters.text: Many large Astana businesses have state or quasi-state shareholders, or connections to politically exposed persons. We map holding structures through Kazakh registry extracts, AIFC records, foreign registers and media, distinguishing documented ownership from indications and stating confidence levels for investment committees.

local_context.title: AIFC Court and arbitration centre
local_context.text: The AIFC Court is independent of Kazakhstan's ordinary judicial system, applies AIFC law drawing on the law of England and Wales, and works in English. It has exclusive jurisdiction over disputes among AIFC participants and bodies, disputes about AIFC-governed operations and cases referred to it by agreement. Together with the International Arbitration Centre it handled 1,282 cases in 2025, including 303 arbitrations.

local_context.title: AIFC regulator and exchange
local_context.text: The Astana Financial Services Authority licenses and supervises financial services within the AIFC, and the Astana International Exchange sets its own listing rules. The AIFC was created under a 2015 Constitutional Statute and offers tax exemptions on qualifying financial services until 2066. AFSA public registers, enforcement notices and AIX disclosures are valuable sources on AIFC participants. Licensing status can change, so registers are checked at the time of each engagement.

local_context.title: National courts and government bodies
local_context.text: Ordinary commercial disputes in Astana go to the city's specialised economic court, with appeals to the Astana City Court; the Supreme Court sits in the capital. Ministries, regulators and procurement bodies are headquartered here, so official decisions, tender results and published court acts are central to research on Astana companies and public contracts. Most records are published in Kazakh and Russian, and some are only available in one of them.

local_context.title: Registries and local enquiries
local_context.text: Companies are registered in the national register of business identification numbers, with extracts through eGov, and AIFC share transactions are notified for that register. Kazakhstan has no enacted law licensing private detectives, as described on our Kazakhstan page. TDSC therefore scopes any local enquiries in Astana with Kazakh counsel and qualified professionals, without covert surveillance or access to state databases.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Astana and works on Astana matters from Nashville. We first agree the purpose with the client's counsel, whether a bid for public works, an investment or partnership with an AIFC participant, a sanctions or export review, or support for AIFC Court or arbitration proceedings. Research uses Kazakh registry extracts, AFSA and AIX disclosures, published court acts, procurement information, foreign corporate records and media in Kazakh, Russian and English. Matters are screened for sanctions compliance given trade links with Russia. Local enquiries are coordinated through Kazakh counsel and qualified professionals, and personal data is handled consistently with Kazakh law or AIFC data protection rules, as applicable.

faqs.q: Are AIFC companies easier to research than other Kazakh companies?
faqs.a: Often yes. AIFC participants are subject to English-language rules, and licensed firms appear in AFSA registers with any public enforcement action, while listed issuers disclose through AIX. Ownership behind AIFC entities can still run through foreign vehicles, so we combine these records with national and foreign registers and media.

faqs.q: Can the AIFC Court hear our dispute with an Astana company?
faqs.a: The AIFC Court hears disputes among AIFC participants, disputes about operations governed by AIFC law, and other civil disputes the parties agree to refer to it; it does not hear criminal or administrative cases. Whether it is available is a question for counsel. We tailor research and reporting to the forum chosen.

faqs.q: How do you assess links between a partner and Kazakh officials?
faqs.a: We research ownership and management history, family and business connections disclosed in registry records, court acts and media, and public information on officials' prior roles. We report documented links separately from unconfirmed indications, so compliance teams and counsel can judge the risk under anti-corruption laws that apply to the client.

faqs.q: Is Astana subject to US sanctions?
faqs.a: Kazakhstan is not a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction. However, some Kazakh companies have been designated or scrutinised for helping Russia obtain controlled goods. TDSC screens every matter for sanctions compliance and researches counterparties' ownership and trade links so clients can make informed export and payment decisions.

faqs.q: Can TDSC conduct investigations on the ground in Astana?
faqs.a: Kazakhstan has no enacted licensing regime for private detectives as of 2026. TDSC does not carry out covert surveillance or seek access to state databases. Where on-the-ground enquiries are needed, we scope them with Kazakh counsel and coordinate qualified local professionals within the current legal framework.
